note: RIDDLER SEAT 6 — the elegist. Riddle: the world is older than the story and will outlive it. Deep time, grief dressed as landscape. Equivalents ride this shelf (Peake, Morris, Eddison).
interactions: Inklings: C.S. Lewis was the reader who demanded the story continue; the pub read-alouds are the shelf's oral tradition
'Beowulf: The Monsters and the Critics' (1936) re-founded Anglo-Saxon studies — the criticism outranked the fiction in the academy
'On Fairy-Stories' (1947) is the theory Le Guin's Earthsea stands on: escape, recovery, consolation (edge: le_guin shelf)
Morris is the direct ancestor of the deep-time register; Eddison praised to the point of envy
Pratchett: The Colour of Magic opens as parody of this shelf's archetypes — the funhouse mirror facing the elegist (edge: pratchett shelf)
